name: Peter: Joppa → Caesarea
summary: Acts 10 links Peter’s stay at Joppa with travel to Cornelius in Caesarea. The line is a generalized coastal/plain corridor.

segments.note: Generalized first-century coastal/plain corridor; Acts does not preserve the exact road alignment.

name: Saul/Paul: Jerusalem → Damascus
summary: Acts gives Jerusalem and Damascus as endpoints but no recoverable approach road or encounter coordinate.

segments.note: Schematic intercity corridor only; the exact Damascus-road route and encounter point are unknown.

name: Philip: Samaria / Gaza road → Azotus → Caesarea
summary: Acts 8 gives a sequence from Samaria to the Jerusalem–Gaza road, then Azotus and coastal towns to Caesarea. The desert-road encounter itself has no exact point.

segments.note: Illustrative regional line only. Acts does not identify the exact starting city in Samaria or the exact desert stretch of the Jerusalem–Gaza road.
Schematic coastal transition; Acts says Philip was found at Azotus but does not narrate a step-by-step road.
Generalized coastal corridor through unnamed towns; not a recovered itinerary.

name: Paul & Barnabas — first missionary journey
summary: Acts 13–14 city sequence from Antioch through Cyprus and southern Anatolia, including the narrated return through Lystra, Iconium, Pisidian Antioch and Perga. Lines are generalized; Derbe is visualized with an explicitly disputed candidate.

segments.note: Generalized descent from Antioch to its port; exact road alignment not claimed.
Illustrative sea crossing; winds and exact sailing track are unknown.
Generalized cross-island corridor; Acts says they traversed the island but does not specify the road.
Illustrative maritime crossing to Pamphylia; exact track unknown.

Acts explicitly revisits Antioch after Iconium; route geometry is schematic.

name: Paul — second missionary journey
summary: Acts 15:40–18:23 from Antioch through Syria/Cilicia, Macedonia and Achaia, then Cenchreae/Ephesus/Caesarea and back to Antioch. Regional and maritime lines remain generalized.

segments.note: Acts names Syria and Cilicia rather than Tarsus as a required stop; this line ends at a broad regional anchor, not a city claim.
Generalized movement into the Derbe/Lystra area. The exact road and whether Tarsus was visited are not stated by Acts.

Acts says Paul “went up and greeted the church” before going down to Antioch, but the verse does not name Jerusalem. The atlas therefore does not force Jerusalem as a plotted waypoint.

name: Paul — Ephesus, Macedonia, and return to Jerusalem
summary: Acts 18:23–21:17 from Antioch through Galatia/Phrygia to Ephesus, then the Macedonia/Greece circuit and the detailed Troas-to-Jerusalem return. Unnamed regional travel is shown with regional anchors rather than invented city stops.

segments.note: Acts names the Galatian region; this ends at a broad regional anchor and is not a city stop or surveyed route.
Broad regional visualization only; “Galatian region and Phrygia” cannot be reduced to one exact road.

summary: Acts 23 provides Jerusalem, Antipatris, and Caesarea as explicit stages; the line follows only a schematic military-road corridor.
